Q1.topic: ND / Not Detected and below LOQ/LOD representation
Q1.question: How should ND / Not Detected and below-LOQ / below-LOD appear on GET /v0/clients/sample/{id} lab_data.categories.*.compounds — omitted row, value 0, empty string, qualifier, distinct token, or other? How do value, lod, loq, and qualifiers interact?
Q1.answer: API returns the lab-saved numeric value in Confident, standardized to the category's canonical unit. A value of 0 can correspond to a COA display of ND/Not Detected. LOD and LOQ are returned separately; downstream consumers must derive any below-limit presentation.

Q2.question: When secondary_report_units is set, does GET ever return a second numeric for the same compound, or only a display conversion / category-level unit hint?
Q2.answer: The API returns exactly one canonical numeric value per test category. primary_report_unit and secondary_report_unit do not create additional numeric results; downstream consumers perform conversions using payload context such as unit weight.

Q3.question: For an ordered/required panel analyte that was not run, is omission the only signal, or can status/qualifiers (or another field) mark not tested / not performed?
Q3.answer: Analytes saved with null values are omitted from the API. Confident's default COA behavior may display NT/Not Tested, though labs may customize presentation.
